req.title: Blog post title required on update
req.statement: The system shall reject POST /<id>/update with a missing title, rendering an error.
triggers: blog post title required on update

doc.reasoning: R-FLASKR-040 requires that POST /<id>/update rejects a missing title by re-rendering the update form with an error message (HTTP 200, not a redirect). Three test cases are designed: (1) positive — valid title+body yields a redirect (302) confirming the happy path; (2) negative — empty title string yields HTTP 200 with 'Title is required.' error text, no DB update; (3) boundary — whitespace-only title (single space) is treated as truthy by Python's `if not title` check, so it passes validation and redirects, confirming the exact boundary of the falsy check. Each test is self-contained, uses the pre-loaded fixture data (user id=1 / 'test'/'test', post id=1), and asserts exact values to maximise mutation kill rate.

tests.name: test_update_with_valid_title_redirects
preconditions: App initialised with TESTING=True and a fresh temp database
Pre-loaded fixture: user id=1 (test/test), post id=1 owned by user 1
User 'test' is logged in via POST /auth/login
actions: POST /1/update with title='Updated Title', body='Updated body'
expected: Database record for post id=1 now has title='Updated Title'
trace: R-FLASKR-040: valid title must be accepted and result in redirect
Catches mutations that flip the redirect vs re-render branch
tests.executable:
import tempfile, os
from flaskr import create_app

def test_update_with_valid_title_redirects():
    fd, path = tempfile.mkstemp()
    os.close(fd)
    app = create_app({'TESTING': True, 'DATABASE': path})
    with app.app_context():
        from flaskr.db import init_db
        init_db()
    client = app.test_client()
    r = client.post('/auth/login', data={'username': 'test', 'password': 'test'})
    assert r.status_code == 302
    r = client.post('/1/update', data={'title': 'Updated Title', 'body': 'Updated body'})
    assert r.status_code == 302
    assert r.headers['Location'] == '/'
    with app.app_context():
        from flaskr.db import get_db
        post = get_db().execute('SELECT title FROM post WHERE id = 1').fetchone()
        assert post['title'] == 'Updated Title'

test_update_with_valid_title_redirects()

from flaskr import create_app

def test_update_empty_title_does_not_redirect():
    fd, path = tempfile.mkstemp()
    os.close(fd)
    app = create_app({'TESTING': True, 'DATABASE': path})
    with app.app_context():
        from flaskr.db import init_db
        init_db()
    client = app.test_client()
    r = client.post('/auth/login', data={'username': 'test', 'password': 'test'})
